info_s1_p1: By default, all traffic goes through the tunnel (AllowedIPs = 0.0.0.0/0). In settings (step 2) you can choose a DNS server and presets — only the required IPv4 subnets will be routed through the tunnel. IPv6 can be enabled optionally, but it increases the route count 2–3× and may cause issues on routers and mobile clients. Safe limit — 1000 IPv4 CIDR.
info_s1_p2: IP ranges can be replaced manually. Up-to-date lists at opencck.org and rockblack.pro.
info_legacy_li2: Masks only the start of the connection
info_legacy_li3: Works with Cloudflare WARP without a server
info_awg2_li1: Dynamic headers + random padding in all packets
info_awg2_li2: Mimics QUIC/DNS throughout the entire session
info_awg2_li3: Harder to detect with heuristic DPI analysis
info_s3_title: Is a server required for AWG 2.0?
info_s3_p1: For Cloudflare WARP — no. Configs from this generator work with Cloudflare's public server without any server-side configuration.
info_s3_p2: For your own server — yes. Self-hosted AWG 2.0 requires an updated kernel/module amneziawg-linux-kernel-module on the server and new client configs (old AWG 1.5 configs become incompatible). See the official documentation for details.
instruction_step1:
Download and install AmneziaWG:
Follow the download link and get the installer for Windows. Install to the default path "C:\Program Files\...".
instruction_step2:
Generate and import the config file:
Choose AWG 1.5, 2.0, 3.0, or 3.1 according to client support. AWG 3.x uses a WARP-safe client profile; AWG 3.1 is recommended with AmneziaVPN 5.0.1.5+ or a compatible client. Download the configuration and import the .conf file into the client.
instruction_conclusion: After importing, enable the tunnel in the client. The client restores its state when Windows starts.

diagnostics_title: What to check if it does not work
diagnostics_no_handshake: If it does not connect: check endpoint, port, UDP availability, AWG mode, and client version.
diagnostics_connected_no_sites: If it connects but websites do not open: check DNS, AllowedIPs, IPv6, and MTU.
diagnostics_wifi_vs_mobile: If it works on Wi-Fi but not on mobile network: try another port, hostname instead of IP, or another endpoint mode.
diagnostics_import_failed: If import fails: check the AWG mode, client parser version, profile format, and import method. AWG 3.0 vpn:// is intentionally unavailable.
routing_mode_full_desc: All supported traffic will be routed through WARP. Use this if you do not need to choose specific services.
routing_mode_split_desc: Only selected destinations will be routed through WARP. If a website is not covered by selected presets, it may bypass the tunnel.
routing_empty_split_error: Choose at least one destination for split tunnel or switch back to full tunnel.
routing_presets_ignored_in_full: Full tunnel is selected. Presets will not limit routes in this mode.
routing_allowedips_full: AllowedIPs will use the default full route. All supported traffic will go through the tunnel.
routing_allowedips_split: AllowedIPs will include only networks from selected destinations. If a website is not covered by selected presets, it may bypass the tunnel.
routing_allowedips_limit: Large AllowedIPs lists may import or work unstably on phones and routers. The generator warns at 80% of the limit and blocks selection at 1000 IPv4 CIDR unless "No limit" is enabled.
routing_allowedips_nolimit: "No limit" removes the safety cap, but it does not guarantee that the client or router will handle a large route list correctly.
routing_allowedips_mobile_ipv6: Mobile profile forces IPv6 off to reduce issues on mobile networks and clients.
onboarding_body: The generator creates a ready AmneziaWG/WARP profile for import into a VPN client. You can download a .conf file or copy vpn:// if your client supports quick import. Full tunnel routes all supported traffic through WARP, while split tunnel routes only selected destinations. Connectivity depends on the client, network, endpoint, DNS, and routes.
onboarding_no_guarantee: The generator reduces manual configuration, but it does not guarantee connectivity in every network or client.

privacy_subtitle: What happens to data during generation
privacy_body:
The awgconfig.com server registers a Cloudflare WARP device for you and immediately returns the finished config. Keys and configs are not stored on the server; only technical errors reach the logs.

Generation history is kept only in this browser (localStorage) — you can clear it in the History window.

Analytics: Yandex Metrica without Webvisor plus anonymous product events (mode, generation outcome). Keys, endpoint addresses and config contents are never sent to analytics.

Third-party services: Cloudflare (WARP registration) and iplist.opencck.org (route lists for split tunnelling).

faq_lead: How the generator works and what to do if the tunnel does not come up.
faq_q1: What is AmneziaWG and how is it different from WireGuard?
faq_a1: AmneziaWG is a WireGuard fork by the Amnezia team. Encryption and keys are the same as in WireGuard, but the protocol adds obfuscation: junk packets before the handshake (Jc, Jmin, Jmax), CPS imitation packets (I1–I5) and, from AWG 2.0 on, header and padding parameters. This makes AmneziaWG traffic harder to identify by the WireGuard signature.
faq_q2: What is Cloudflare WARP and do I need my own server?
faq_a2: WARP is a free Cloudflare service built on WireGuard. The generator registers a new device through the official WARP API and builds a ready config from the result, so no server of your own is needed. The Cloudflare server stays a standard WireGuard peer, which is why some AmneziaWG parameters are intentionally fixed for it: S1–S4 = 0, H1–H4 = 1–4, MTU 1280.
faq_q3: Which profile should I choose: AWG 1.5, 2.0, 3.0 or 3.1?
faq_a3: Start with AWG 2.0: it is the default and imports into current AmneziaWG and AmneziaVPN. AWG 1.5 is for older clients. AWG 3.0 and 3.1 add client-side features of newer versions such as timing randomization; 3.1 needs AmneziaVPN 5.0.1.5+ or a compatible client. If the import fails, go back to AWG 2.0.
faq_q4: How do I import the config into AmneziaWG or AmneziaVPN?
faq_a4: On Windows, install the AmneziaWG client and add a tunnel from the downloaded .conf file. On Android and iOS, use AmneziaVPN or AmneziaWG: import the .conf file or paste the vpn:// link if it is available for the chosen profile. For routers (Keenetic, OpenWrt, MikroTik, GL.iNet), turn on "Router mode" in settings before generating.
faq_q5: The config imports but does not connect. What should I do?
faq_a5: Try another UDP port (2408, 500, 1701) and an endpoint IP address instead of the hostname — both are in the settings of step 2. On mobile networks, turn on the mobile profile. Make sure your client version supports the chosen AWG profile. If it connects but sites do not open, check DNS and routes. The current service state is on the Status page.
faq_q6: Is it free? What happens to the keys?
faq_a6: The generator is free and needs no sign-up. Keys are created during generation and handed straight to you — the server does not store them. Generation history is kept only in your browser and can be cleared. The source code is open under the AGPL-3.0 license.
faq_q7: Can I route only some sites through WARP?
faq_a7: Yes. In settings, choose split routing and tick the services you need: only their IPv4 subnets go into AllowedIPs, and other traffic goes directly. To keep the config reliable on phones and routers, the generator limits the list to 1000 IPv4 subnets.
